title: Arguments grid: for and against
subject: English

source: Written for english/y9 lesson 54 (Arguments grid: for and against (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 54: Non-fiction: ethics in a time of war. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: For showing images
Against
rows: images tell the truth when words fail
they can strip people of dignity
they have moved the public to demand change
the people shown cannot give consent
they keep a record for history
constant images can make viewers numb

passage.title: 'The Picture and the Person', a teacher-written article for TGA
paras: A photograph of suffering should be published only if it serves the people in it: if it tells their truth, protects their dignity and asks something of us. Otherwise it is not journalism. It is just looking.

model.title: How convincing is the article's conclusion?

parts.text: Point: the conclusion is convincing because it is conditional, not extreme
Evidence: 'only if it serves the people in it'
Explain: it keeps truth and dignity together
Develop: but who decides what 'serves' them?
Link: a strong argument still leaves hard questions

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The conclusion is convincing because it sets conditions instead of choosing an extreme: a picture should be published 'only if it serves the people in it'. However, it leaves open who decides what serves them, so the argument is persuasive but not complete.

keywords.def: ideas about what is right and wrong
the worth and respect every person deserves
giving fair weight to different sides

questions.q: Summarise one argument for and one against in your own words
questions.a: For: images reveal truth and can move people to act. Against: they can take away dignity without consent.

questions.q: Find the short sentence that ends the article and explain its effect
questions.a: 'It is just looking.': blunt and short, it condemns careless publishing.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'How convincing is the writer's argument?' Starter: 'The writer's argument is convincing because...'
questions.a: A PEEDL paragraph evaluating the conclusion, with a counter-point.

questions.q: Extend: link the article to War Photographer in one sentence
questions.a: For example: 'Satyamurti's speaker feels the weight the article describes: the person in the picture matters more than the picture.'

questions.q: Stretch: write a short reply to the writer, agreeing or disagreeing
questions.a: A reasoned reply with one counter-argument answered.

questions.q: What is the writer's final viewpoint?
options: publish only when it serves and respects the people shown
questions.a: C) publish only when it serves and respects the people shown. The conclusion sets conditions rather than choosing an extreme.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: should the world see photographs of suffering?
questions.a: A judgement with a condition, e.g. only with dignity and purpose.
